# Oversized inline drawings and invisible tails

Original XML/pixels generated by `tools/inline_soft_hyphens_fixture.py --mode 14`
and `--mode 15`. Sixteen cases per mode cover plain oversized pictures, terminal
and repeated soft hyphens, following words/spaces/manual breaks, fitting pictures,
effect extents and equivalent drawing groups. No user artwork is copied.

The reference application exported the exact sources read-only. The fixture-specific
`tools/export-inline-soft-hyphens.ps1` bypasses SmartArt traversal because these
sources contain none; the reference application exposes cyclic GroupItems COM enumeration for these
simple one-child groups. `tools/record_inline_soft_hyphens.py` records PDF/source
hashes and raw native text origins without importing engine geometry.

Mode 14 starts invisible tails after oversized drawings on another line. Mode 15
keeps trailing soft hyphens/spaces on the drawing line; following visible text and
manual breaks still advance. Both modes retain identical physical picture sizes.
The browser test checks all sixteen pages in each mode within 0.15pt,
plus editing, exact no-edit/undo package contents and editable reopening.

Page eight (fitting picture plus a visible discretionary hyphen) previously
placed following baselines about 3.2pt too low in both modes. The line builder
now retains the optional hyphen's identity for picture-only metrics, while still
painting its glyph. Both cases pass normally, together with the 24 additional
font-size/picture-height/literal-hyphen controls in `discretionary-hyphen-metrics`.

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.3.29 specifies invisible unused optional hyphens and visible
hyphens at chosen breaks; §20.4.2.6–8 defines effects, extent and inline placement.
The mode-dependent overflow policy is native compatibility behavior, not a claimed
contradiction of an explicit overflow rule. Other spacing modes and complex-script
interaction are not established by this matrix.
